title: The Speed-Accuracy-Energy Pareto Frontier in Deliberative Biological Nervous Systems and Synthetic Reasoning Models
plain_title: Thinking longer costs energy, in brains and AI
thesis: Brains and AI reasoning models both cut their mistakes by thinking longer, and both pay for it in time and energy along a measurable speed-accuracy-energy trade-off.
summary: The paper compiles 17 empirical decision-making benchmarks (including 10 paired fast-versus-deliberative speed-accuracy curves) from ultra-fast insect reflexes to rat maze replay, crow tool inspection, ant and honeybee nest quorums, human math competition solving and frontier AI test-time reasoning, alongside all 33 substrates in the hardware table. Across the paired experiments, extending deliberation time consistently boosts log-odds accuracy while multiplying energy cost by active power. Comparing a full AI reasoning run on an 8-GPU node against a human solving the same competition math problem reveals a 56-to-70-fold macroscopic energy gap rooted in synaptic versus GPU+DRAM physics.

claims.claim: A test-time AI reasoning run on an eight-H100 node spends 672 kilojoules (OpenAI o1) to 840 kilojoules (DeepSeek-R1) per competition math problem.
claims.paper_value: 8 × 700 W = 5.60 kW node: OpenAI o1 runs 120 s = 6.72×10⁵ J (~82 J per token, lifting AIME accuracy from 9.3% to 74.4%); DeepSeek-R1 runs 150 s = 8.40×10⁵ J (lifting AIME accuracy from 39.2% to 79.8%)
claims.data_value: 5,600 W × 120 s = 6.72×10⁵ J (9.3% → 74.4%) and 5,600 W × 150 s = 8.40×10⁵ J (39.2% → 79.8%) in deliberation_speed_accuracy_energy.csv; 700 W per H100 matches cleaned_hardware_benchmarks.csv
claims.note: Revised on 24 November 2026: all sections, Table 1 and Figures 1–3 use the exact 5.60 kW 8×H100 node budget.

claims.claim: Solving a 10-minute competition math problem on a 20-watt human brain takes 12 kilojoules — making current AI test-time reasoning 56 to 70 times (1.75 to 1.85 orders of magnitude) more energy-intensive per problem.
claims.paper_value: human 20.0 W × 600 s = 12.0 kJ versus 672 kJ (OpenAI o1, 56.0× = 1.75 orders) and 840 kJ (DeepSeek-R1, 70.0× = 1.85 orders)
claims.source: deliberation_speed_accuracy_energy.csv (human AIME, OpenAI o1 and DeepSeek-R1 rows)
claims.note: Revised on 24 November 2026: the earlier contradiction between '56-fold' and 'five orders of magnitude' was resolved everywhere in favour of the exact 56× to 70× macroscopic ratio.

claims.claim: At the substrate level, an H100 arithmetic operation costs 71 times more energy than a local cortical postsynaptic event, while an off-chip HBM3 memory fetch costs 20,000 times more.
claims.paper_value: local cortical synapse 0.010 pJ (1.0×10¹⁴ ops/J; versus 0.133 pJ whole-brain amortized human budget = 7.5×10¹² ops/J); Nvidia H100 MAC 0.708 pJ (70.8× local synapse, 5.3× whole-brain amortized); HBM3 DRAM fetch 200 pJ (20,000× local synapse)
claims.data_value: 1.00×10⁻¹⁴ J (cortical synapse), 7.08×10⁻¹³ J (H100) and 2.00×10⁻¹⁰ J (DRAM) in cleaned_hardware_benchmarks.csv; 20 W ÷ 1.50×10¹⁴/s = 1.33×10⁻¹³ J in neural_sensory_evolution_timeseries.csv
claims.note: Both the local cleft energy (0.010 pJ) and the whole-brain amortized synaptic budget (0.133 pJ) are explicitly distinguished and match both project tables.

claims.claim: Across all 10 paired fast-versus-slow deliberation experiments in the dataset, investing more decision time reliably raises accuracy (log-odds slope 0.54, R² = 0.67 across interior pairs).
claims.paper_value: 10 of 10 paired tasks show positive accuracy gain (sign test p = 9.77×10⁻⁴); across N = 9 interior probability pairs, log-odds gain = (0.5395 ± 0.1420) × ln(T_slow ÷ T_fast) + 0.5725 (R² = 0.6734, p = 0.0067; all N = 10 slope 0.5695 ± 0.1905, R² = 0.5275)
claims.data_value: exact ordinary-least-squares fit on the paired columns of deliberation_speed_accuracy_energy.csv reproduces slope 0.5395 ± 0.1420, intercept 0.5725, R² = 0.6734 (N = 9) and 0.5695 ± 0.1905, R² = 0.5275 (N = 10)
claims.note: Revised on 24 November 2026: replaced the earlier unreproducible 25-row fit with an exact empirical regression on the 10 paired SAT benchmarks.

claims.claim: The incremental energy spent per bit of error reduction spans more than nine orders of magnitude from fruit-fly sensory integration to frontier LLM reasoning.
claims.paper_value: 9.41 orders of magnitude, from 1.94×10⁻⁴ J per bit of error reduction in Drosophila FoxP olfactory integration up to 5.02×10⁵ J per bit in DeepSeek-R1 math reasoning
claims.data_value: recomputed directly from (E_delib − E_fast) ÷ ΔI_err across the paired rows of deliberation_speed_accuracy_energy.csv: min 1.94×10⁻⁴ J/bit, max 5.02×10⁵ J/bit (span 9.41 orders)
claims.note: Every energy-per-bit value is now computed directly from measured latencies, error rates and power budgets in the ledger.

rationale.step: Ballistic reflexes minimise latency (0.13 to 7.5 ms) and energy (nanojoules to microjoules) on stereotyped triggers, whereas novel or noisy choices require sequential evidence accumulation.
rationale.note: Directly anchored by the four reflex benchmarks and ten paired speed-accuracy tasks in deliberation_speed_accuracy_energy.csv.

rationale.step: Across 10 paired biological and silicon benchmarks, multiplying deliberation time consistently increases log-odds choice accuracy while scaling energy dissipation as power × time.
rationale.note: Verified by the reproducible log-odds regression (slope 0.54 ± 0.14, R² = 0.67, p = 0.0067) on the 10 paired rows.

rationale.step: Autoregressive reasoning tokens and tree search in AI perform an analogous test-time accuracy-for-energy trade-off to biological evidence accumulation and replay.
rationale.note: Both AlphaZero MCTS and o1/R1 reasoning chains fall cleanly along the same positive log-odds accuracy-vs-time trend in the ledger, with functional differences noted explicitly.

rationale.step: Current GPU clusters spend 56 to 70 times more energy than a human brain on a competition math problem because off-chip memory movement (200 pJ) and dense MACs (0.71 pJ) far exceed synaptic costs (0.01 to 0.133 pJ).
rationale.note: Both the macroscopic task ratio (672–840 kJ vs 12 kJ) and the microscopic substrate costs come straight from the project's two benchmark CSVs.

conclusions.conclusion: Extending test-time computation reliably reduces error across insects, rodents, birds, primates, social insect colonies and reasoning LLMs, at a proportional thermodynamic cost.
conclusions.note: Supported across 10/10 paired empirical benchmarks in deliberation_speed_accuracy_energy.csv.

conclusions.conclusion: Frontier AI reasoning on 8×H100 nodes currently consumes 56 to 70 times (~1.8 orders of magnitude) more energy per math competition problem than a human brain.
conclusions.note: Directly computed from 5.60 kW × 120–150 s (672–840 kJ) versus 20 W × 600 s (12 kJ).

conclusions.conclusion: Closing the silicon deliberation energy gap requires co-locating weights and compute to eliminate the 20,000-fold off-chip DRAM energy penalty relative to cortical synapses.
conclusions.note: Directly grounded in the 33-substrate hardware table (200 pJ HBM3 fetch vs 0.010 pJ local synapse and 0.40 pJ IBM NorthPole near-memory silicon).

bottom_line: Following the 24 November 2026 revision, every benchmark row, speed-accuracy curve, GPU power budget (5.60 kW → 672 kJ for o1 and 840 kJ for DeepSeek-R1), human-versus-AI ratio (56× to 70×), substrate energy comparison, catalog ID and figure in Paper 3 is computed directly from deliberation_speed_accuracy_energy.csv and cleaned_hardware_benchmarks.csv.
